name: Grit-tempered pottery at Taperinha
description: Excavators recovered fragile, grit-tempered bowl fragments from the Taperinha riverine shell midden near Santarém. Fish, turtle and especially freshwater mussel remains in the midden indicate intensive riverine foraging.

impact.note: Pottery was a new ability for this fishing community, but it is one site and no later tradition is known to descend from it.

date.label: 7600–7280 cal BP (c. 5650–5330 BCE)
date.basis: Roosevelt et al. Table 1 reports this 95% range for reduced carbon from sherd OxA-2431 in the base of level 12. The paper gives an older age for some associated charcoal and shell.

events.statement: A grit-tempered sherd from the base of level 12 in Test 1 yielded a reduced-carbon AMS date. Another piece of the same sherd yielded a much less precise thermoluminescence age.

evidence.supports: Table 1 identifies the dated sherd and carbon fractions. Table 2 and Fig. 5 show their excavation context.
Reports grit-tempered pottery, the TL assay on part of the same sherd, and possible dating biases.

events.place_note: Taperinha shell midden near Santarém, Pará
events.caveats: The two carbon fractions and the thermoluminescence measurement come from one sherd. The authors discuss potential contamination and uncertain environmental parameters.

earliest_record.rationale: This anchor uses the ceramic-specific reduced-carbon determination. Older shell and charcoal dates characterize other levels or deposits.

caveats: The dated sherd and associated sediments use different dating materials and methods. The contents and uses of the vessels remain uncertain.

unresolved.note: The inspected abstract does not settle independent invention versus transmission.

research.note: The original excavation and full dating tables were read. The deposit supports aquatic-resource use but does not establish what the pottery held.
